## Registration of `browser.start`

- `Browser.start` in `browser.py` is decorated with `@command.command("browser.start")`. That decorator is what registers the command.
- The `Browser` class is instantiated in the default addon list in `mitmproxy/addons/__init__.py`, in `default_addons()`, as `browser.Browser()`. The addon manager collects its decorated commands when it loads.
- The console UI binds the `B` key to it in `mitmproxy/tools/console/defaultkeys.py`: `km.add("B", "browser.start", ["global"], "Start an attached browser")`.
- `start(browser: str = "chrome")` dispatches on the name:
  - `chrome` or `chromium` goes to `Browser.launch_chrome`.
  - `firefox` goes to `Browser.launch_firefox`.
  - Anything else logs "Invalid browser name."
- If a browser is already running, it logs "Starting additional browser", and the new one is added to the list.

## Finding the executable

Two helpers do the lookup:
- `find_executable_cmd(*search_paths)` returns `[path]` for the first candidate where `shutil.which` succeeds. That works for both absolute paths and bare names on `PATH`.
- `find_flatpak_cmd(*search_paths)` requires `flatpak` on `PATH`. It runs `flatpak info <id>` for each candidate, and on the first exit code 0 it returns `["flatpak", "run", "-p", id]`.

Each launcher tries native executables first and falls back to Flatpak:

| Browser | Candidates in `find_executable_cmd`, in order | Flatpak IDs |
|---|---|---|
| Chrome (`launch_chrome`) | macOS `/Applications/Google Chrome.app/.../Google Chrome`; two Windows `chrome.exe` paths under `C:\Program Files (x86)`; then `google-chrome`, `google-chrome-stable`, `chrome`, `chromium`, `chromium-browser`, `google-chrome-unstable` | `com.google.Chrome`, `org.chromium.Chromium`, `com.github.Eloston.UngoogledChromium`, `com.google.ChromeDev` |
| Firefox (`launch_firefox`) | macOS `/Applications/Firefox.app/Contents/MacOS/firefox`; Windows `C:\Program Files\Mozilla Firefox\firefox.exe`; then `firefox`, `mozilla-firefox`, `mozilla` | `org.mozilla.firefox` |

If nothing is found, it logs "Your platform is not supported yet - please submit a patch." and returns.

## Flags and isolation

**Chrome** (`launch_chrome`) starts with a fresh `tempfile.TemporaryDirectory()` as the profile, which is what isolates it. The `Popen` arguments are:
- `--user-data-dir=<tmpdir>`
- `--proxy-server=<listen_host or 127.0.0.1>:<listen_port or 8080>`, read from `ctx.options`
- `--disable-fre`, `--no-default-browser-check` and `--no-first-run`, which skip first-run and default-browser prompts
- `--disable-extensions`
- `about:blank` as the start page

**Firefox** (`launch_firefox`) has no proxy command-line flag, so it writes a `prefs.js` into a new temp profile directory and launches with `--profile <tmpdir> --new-window about:blank`. The prefs include:
- `network.proxy.type = 1` (manual proxy) and `share_proxy_settings = true`.
- `network.proxy.http` / `http_port` and `network.proxy.ssl` / `ssl_port`, set from the listen host and port in the `for service in ("http", "ssl")` loop.
- Many prefs that disable telemetry, updates, Normandy/Shield studies, Safe Browsing, region lookup, Pocket, captive-portal and connectivity checks, push, remote settings, and the new-tab sponsored sites and bookmarks.

**Bug in the pref list:** in `launch_firefox`, the lines for `app.shield.optoutstudies.enabled` and `extensions.blocklist.enabled` are missing a comma. Python concatenates them into one list element. It is harmless because `writelines` adds no newlines anyway. But the prefs are all written on a single line with no separators, and Firefox still parses them.

Both launchers send stdout and stderr to `DEVNULL`.

## Lifecycle

- `Browser.browser` and `Browser.tdir` are class-level lists that track the processes and temp dirs.
- `Browser.done()` runs when the addon shuts down. It kills every process, calls `cleanup()` on every temp dir to delete the profiles, and resets both lists.
